name: Elishua
overview: Elishua is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified in Scripture as a son of King David. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, emphasizing his place within the royal lineage of Israel. There are no additional notes or details about his life or deeds in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishua means 'G-d is my salvation,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew meaning that honors God's role in deliverance. Another related name, Elishama, meaning 'G-d has heard,' is also associated with David's lineage, showing a pattern of names that express trust and communication with God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elishua as a son of David, establishing him within the royal family of Israel. Beyond this direct filial relationship, no other family connections or descendants are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elishua's significance lies in his inclusion among David's sons, contributing to the genealogical record that underscores the fulfillment of God's promises to David's house. His presence in the lineage highlights the continuity of God's covenant with Judah and the Davidic line, which ultimately points forward to the coming of the Messiah. Although not a central figure in narrative events, Elishua's role as a royal son situates him within the broader redemptive history recorded in Scripture.
